in_text_mentions: Hair shaft thickness heterogeneity (Figure 2a) is a typical trichoscopic sign of AGA. In the majority of studies included in the analysis, a hair shaft thickness heterogeneity over 20% in men and over 10% in women was considered as a diagnostic criterion for AGA. However, in some publications, the definition of hair diameter diversity was not determined.
Vellus hairs (Figure 2b) were less commonly studied in patients with AGA compared to the other trichoscopic features. They were described in 13 articles and examined in 775 patients.

The peripilar sign (Figure 2c), also known as perifollicular hyperpigmentation, was studied in 24 out of 34 selected articles. Based on our results, the mean frequency of the peripilar sign in patients with AGA was 43.27% with the incidence rate between 9.70% and 100%. The peripilar sign was more common in men (63.67%) than women (42.53%) (Table 1). The analysis showed that the calculated specificity was the highest among all the features (96.06%). The positive predictive value was also considerable at 95.76% (Table 1).
